sentences.zh: 徐州彭城郡彭城郡舊置徐州，後齊置東南道行台，後周立總管府。

translations.literal: Xuzhou, Pengcheng Commandery: Pengcheng Commandery formerly had Xuzhou established there; Later Qi established the Southeast Circuit field headquarters; Later Zhou established a grand administrative office.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou, Pengcheng Commandery. Pengcheng Commandery formerly had Xuzhou established there; Later Qi established the Southeast Circuit field headquarters; Later Zhou established a grand administrative office.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年行台廢，大業四年府廢。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang year seven, the field headquarters was abolished; in Daye year four, the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The field headquarters was abolished in Kaihuang 7, and the office was abolished in Daye 4.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戸一十三萬二百三十二。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 11 counties with a registered population of 130,232 households.

sentences.zh: 彭城舊置郡，後周並沛及南陽平二郡入。開皇初郡廢，大業初複置郡。有呂梁山、徐山。蘄梁置蘄郡。後齊置仁州，又析置龍亢郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢。谷陽後齊置谷陽郡，開皇初郡廢。又有巳吾、義城二縣，後齊並以爲臨淮縣，大業初併入焉。沛留後齊廢，開皇十六年複。有微山、黃山。豐蕭舊置沛郡，後齊廢爲承高縣。開皇六年改爲龍城，十八年改爲臨沛，大業初改曰蕭。有相山。滕舊曰蕃，置蕃郡。後齊廢。開皇十六年改曰滕縣。蘭陵舊曰承，置蘭陵郡。開皇初郡廢，十六年分承置鄶州及蘭陵縣。大業初州廢，又並蘭陵、鄶城二縣入焉，尋改承爲蘭陵。有抱犢山。符離後齊置睢南郡，開皇初郡廢，有竹邑縣，梁置睢州，開皇三年州廢，又廢竹邑入焉。有女山、定陶山。方與後齊廢，開皇十六年複。魯郡舊兗州，大業二年改爲魯郡。

translations.literal: Pengcheng formerly had a commandery established there. Later Zhou merged Pei and Nanyangping commanderies into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. It had Luliang Mountain and Xu Mountain. Qi had Qi Commandery established by Liang. Later Qi established Renzhou there and also divided off Longkang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Guyang had Guyang Commandery established by Later Qi, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It also had Siwu and Yicheng counties; Later Qi made both Linhuai County, and at the beginning of Daye they were merged into Guyang. Pei and Liu had been abolished by Later Qi and were restored in Kaihuang year sixteen. They had Wei Mountain and Huang Mountain. Feng and Xiao formerly had Pei Commandery established there; Later Qi abolished it and made it Chenggao County. In Kaihuang year six it was changed to Longcheng; in year eighteen it was changed to Linpei; at the beginning of Daye it was changed to Xiao. It had Xiang Mountain. Teng was formerly called Fan and had Fan Commandery established there. Later Qi abolished it. In Kaihuang year sixteen it was changed to Teng County. Lanling was formerly called Cheng and had Lanling Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year sixteen Cheng was divided to establish Kuaizhou and Lanling County. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Lanling and Kuaicheng counties were also merged into it; soon Cheng was changed to Lanling. It had Baodu Mountain. Fuli had Suinan Commandery established by Later Qi, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had Zhuyi County; Liang established Suizhou, and in Kaihuang year three the province was abolished and Zhuyi was also abolished into Fuli. It had Nu Mountain and Dingtao Mountain. Fangyu was abolished by Later Qi and restored in Kaihuang year sixteen. Lu Commandery was formerly Yanzhou; in Daye year two it was changed to Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 方與魯郡魯郡舊兗州，改爲魯郡。

translations.literal: Fangyu. Lu Commandery: Lu Commandery was formerly Yan Province and was changed to Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu. Lu Commandery. Lu Commandery was formerly Yan Province and was changed to Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 統縣十，戸十二萬四千一十九。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 10 counties with a registered population of 124,019 households.

sentences.zh: 瑕丘舊廢，開皇十三年複，帶郡。任城舊置高平郡，開皇初廢。鄒有鄒山、承匡山。曲阜舊曰魯郡，後齊改郡爲任城。開皇三年郡廢，四年改縣曰汶陽，十六年改名曲阜。泗水開皇十六年置。有陪尾山、尼丘山、防山。有洙、泗水。平陸後齊曰樂平，開皇十六年改焉。龔丘後齊曰平原縣，開皇十六年改焉。梁父有龜山。博城舊曰博，置泰山郡。後齊改郡曰東平，又並博平、牟入焉。開皇初郡廢，十六年改縣曰汶陽，尋改曰博城。有奉高縣，開皇六年改曰岱山，大業初州廢，又廢岱山縣入焉。有岱山、玉符山。嬴開皇十六年分置牟城縣，大業初併入焉。有艾山。有淄水。琅邪郡舊置北徐州，後周改曰沂州。

translations.literal: Xiaqiu had long been abolished and was restored in Kaihuang year thirteen, carrying the commandery. Rencheng formerly had Gaoping Commandery established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Zou had Zou Mountain and Chengkuang Mountain. Qufu was formerly called Lu Commandery; Later Qi changed the commandery to Rencheng. In Kaihuang year three the commandery was abolished; in year four the county was changed to Wenyang; in year sixteen its name was changed to Qufu. Sishui was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Peiwei Mountain, Niqiu Mountain, and Fang Mountain. It had the Zhu and Si rivers. Pinglu was called Leping under Later Qi and was changed in Kaihuang year sixteen. Gongqiu was called Pingyuan County under Later Qi and was changed in Kaihuang year sixteen. Liangfu had Gui Mountain. Bocheng was formerly called Bo and had Taishan Commandery established there. Later Qi changed the commandery to Dongping and also merged Boping and Mou into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year sixteen the county was changed to Wenyang, and soon changed to Bocheng. It had Fenggao County, which in Kaihuang year six was changed to Daishan; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Daishan County was also abolished into it. It had Dai Mountain and Yufu Mountain. Ying had Moucheng County divided off and established in Kaihuang year sixteen; at the beginning of Daye it was merged into Ying. It had Ai Mountain and the Zi River. Langya Commandery formerly had Northern Xuzhou established; Later Zhou changed it to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戸六萬三千四百二十三。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 7 counties with a registered population of 63,423 households.

sentences.zh: 臨沂舊曰即丘，帶郡。開皇初郡廢，十六年分置臨沂，大業初並即丘入焉。有大祠山。費顓臾舊曰南城武陽，開皇十八年改名焉。又有南城縣，後齊廢。有開明山。新泰後齊廢蒙陰縣入焉。沂水舊置南青州及東安郡，後周改州爲莒州。開皇初郡廢，改縣曰東安。十六年又改曰沂水。大業初州廢。東安後齊廢，開皇十六年複。有松山。莒舊置東莞郡。後齊廢，後置義唐郡。開皇初廢。東海郡梁置南、北二青州，東魏改爲海州。

translations.literal: Linyi was formerly called Jiqiu and carried the commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year sixteen Linyi was separately established; at the beginning of Daye, Jiqiu was merged into it. It had Daci Mountain. Fei and Zhuanyu were formerly called Nanchengwuyang; in Kaihuang year eighteen the name was changed. There was also Nancheng County, which Later Qi abolished. It had Kaiming Mountain. Xintai had Mengyin County abolished into it by Later Qi. Yishui formerly had Southern Qingzhou and Dong'an Commandery established there; Later Zhou changed the province to Juzhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Dong'an. In year sixteen it was again changed to Yishui. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Dong'an was abolished by Later Qi and restored in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Song Mountain. Ju formerly had Dongguan Commandery established there. Later Qi abolished it; later Yitang Commandery was established. It was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Donghai Commandery had Southern and Northern Qingzhou established by Liang; Eastern Wei changed it to Haizhou.

translations.idiomatic: Ju. Former Donghai Commandery. Donghai Commandery—in the Liang dynasty, Southern and Northern Qing Provinces were established; Eastern Wei changed it to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣五，戸二萬七千八百五十八。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 5 counties with a registered population of 27,858 households.

sentences.zh: 朐山舊曰朐，置琅邪郡。後周改縣曰朐山，郡曰朐山。開皇初郡廢，大業初複，帶郡。有朐山、羽山。東海舊置廣饒縣及東海郡，後齊分廣饒置東海縣。開皇初廢郡及東海縣，仁壽元年，改廣饒曰東海。有謝祿山、郁林山。漣水舊曰襄賁。置東海郡。東魏改曰海安。開皇初郡廢，縣又改焉。沭陽梁置潼陽郡。東魏改曰沭陽郡，置縣曰懷文。後周改縣曰沭陽。開皇初郡廢。懷仁梁置南、北二青州。東魏廢州，立義唐郡及懷仁縣。開皇初郡廢。下邳郡後魏置南徐州，梁改爲東徐州，東魏又改曰東楚州，陳改爲安州，後周改爲泗州。

translations.literal: Qushan was formerly called Qu and had Langya Commandery established there. Later Zhou changed the county to Qushan and the commandery to Qushan. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye it was restored and carried the commandery. It had Qushan and Yu Mountain. Donghai formerly had Guangrao County and Donghai Commandery established there; Later Qi divided Guangrao to establish Donghai County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery and Donghai County were abolished; in Renshou year one Guangrao was changed to Donghai. It had Xielu Mountain and Yulin Mountain. Lianshui was formerly called Xiangben and had Donghai Commandery established there. Eastern Wei changed it to Hai'an. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and the county was again changed. Shuyang had Tongyang Commandery established by Liang. Eastern Wei changed it to Shuyang Commandery and established the county as Huaiwen. Later Zhou changed the county to Shuyang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Huairen had Southern and Northern Qingzhou established by Liang. Eastern Wei abolished the provinces and established Yitang Commandery and Huairen County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Xiapi Commandery had Southern Xuzhou established by Later Wei; Liang changed it to Eastern Xuzhou; Eastern Wei again changed it to Eastern Chuzhou; Chen changed it to Anzhou; Later Zhou changed it to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戸五萬二千七十。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 7 counties with a registered population of 52,070 households.

sentences.zh: 宿豫舊置宿豫郡，開皇初郡廢。大業初置下邳郡。又梁置朝陽、臨沭二郡，後齊置晉寧郡，尋並廢。夏丘後齊置，並置夏丘郡，尋立潼州。後周改州爲宋州，縣曰晉陵。開皇初郡廢，十八年州廢，縣複曰夏丘。又東魏置臨潼郡，睢陵縣，後齊改郡爲潼郡。又梁置潼州，後齊改曰睢州，尋廢，亦入潼郡。開皇初郡縣並廢。徐城梁置高平郡。東魏又並梁東平、陽平、清河、歸義四郡爲高平縣，又並梁硃沛、循儀、安豐三郡置硃沛縣。又有安遠郡，後齊廢，後周又並硃沛入高平。開皇初郡廢，十八年更名徐城。淮陽梁置淮陽郡。東魏並綏化、呂梁二郡置綏化縣。後周改縣爲淮陽。開皇初郡廢。又有梁臨清、天水、浮陽三郡，東魏並爲甬城縣，後齊改曰文城縣，後周又改爲臨清，開皇三年省入焉。下邳梁曰歸政，置武州，下邳郡。魏改縣爲下邳，置郡不改，改州曰東徐。後周改州爲邳州。開皇初郡廢，大業初州廢。有嶧山、磬石山。良城梁置武安郡，開皇初郡廢，十一年縣更名曰良城。有徐山。郯舊置郡，開皇初廢。

translations.literal: Suyu formerly had Suyu Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Xiapi Commandery was established. Liang also established Chaoyang and Linshu commanderies; Later Qi established Jinning Commandery; soon all were abolished. Xiaqiu was established by Later Qi, and Xiaqiu Commandery was also established; soon Tongzhou was established. Later Zhou changed the province to Songzhou and called the county Jinling. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year eighteen the province was abolished and the county was again called Xiaqiu. Eastern Wei also established Lintong Commandery and Suiling County; Later Qi changed the commandery to Tong Commandery. Liang also established Tongzhou; Later Qi changed it to Suizhou; it was soon abolished and also entered Tong Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang both commandery and county were abolished. Xucheng had Gaoping Commandery established by Liang. Eastern Wei also merged Liang's four commanderies Dongping, Yangping, Qinghe, and Guiyi to make Gaoping County, and merged Liang's three commanderies Zhupei, Xunyi, and Anfeng to establish Zhupei County. It also had Anyuan Commandery, which Later Qi abolished; Later Zhou also merged Zhupei into Gaoping. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the name was changed to Xucheng. Huaiyang had Huaiyang Commandery established by Liang. Eastern Wei merged Suihua and Luliang commanderies to establish Suihua County. Later Zhou changed the county to Huaiyang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. There were also Liang's Linqing, Tianshui, and Fuyang commanderies; Eastern Wei merged them as Yongcheng County; Later Qi changed it to Wencheng County; Later Zhou again changed it to Linqing, and in Kaihuang year three it was abolished into Huaiyang. Xiapi was called Guizheng by Liang, which established Wuzhou and Xiapi Commandery there. Wei changed the county to Xiapi, left the commandery unchanged, and changed the province to Eastern Xu. Later Zhou changed the province to Pizhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Yi Mountain and Qingshi Mountain. Liangcheng had Wu'an Commandery established by Liang; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eleven the county's name was changed to Liangcheng. It had Xu Mountain. Tan formerly had a commandery established there, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 江陽舊曰廣陵，後齊置廣陵、江陽二郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年改縣爲邗江，大業初。更名江陽。有江都宮、揚子宮。有陵湖。江都自梁及隋，或廢或置。海陵梁置海陵郡。開皇初郡廢，又並建陵縣入，尋析置江浦縣，大業初省入。甯海開皇初並如皋縣入。高郵梁析置竹塘、三歸二縣，及置廣業郡，尋以有嘉禾，爲神農郡。開皇初郡廢，又並竹塘、三歸、臨澤三縣入焉。安宜梁置陽平郡及東莞郡。開皇初郡廢，又廢石鱉縣入焉。有白馬湖。山陽舊置山陽郡，開皇初郡廢。十二年置楚州，大業初州廢。有後魏淮陰郡，東魏改爲淮州，後齊並魯、富陵立懷恩縣，後周改曰壽張，又僑立東平郡。開皇元年改郡爲淮陰，並立楚州，尋廢郡，更改縣曰淮陰。大業初州廢，縣併入焉。盱眙舊魏置盱眙郡。陳置北譙州，尋省。開皇初郡廢，又並考城、直瀆、陽城三縣入。有都梁山。鹽城後齊置射陽郡，陳改曰鹽城，開皇初郡廢。清流舊曰頓丘，置新昌郡及南譙州。開皇初改爲滁州，郡廢。又廢樂钜、高塘二縣入頓丘，改曰新昌。十八年又改爲清流。大業初州廢。有白禪山、曲亭山。全椒梁曰北譙，置北譙郡。後齊改郡爲臨滁，後周又曰北譙。開皇初郡廢，改縣爲滁水。大業初改名焉。有銅官山、九斗山。六合舊曰尉氏，置秦郡。後齊置秦州。後周改州曰方州，改郡曰六合。開皇初郡廢，四年改尉氏曰六合，省堂邑、方山二縣入焉。大業初州廢。又後齊置瓦梁郡，陳廢。有瓜步山、六合山。永福舊曰沛，梁置涇城、東陽二郡，陳廢州，並二郡爲梁郡。後周改梁郡爲石樑郡，改沛縣曰石樑縣，省橫山縣入焉。開皇初郡廢。大業初改縣曰永福。有香山、永福山。句容有茅山、浮山、四平山。延陵舊置南徐州、南東海郡，梁改曰蘭陵郡，陳又改爲東海。開皇九年州郡並廢，又廢丹徒縣入焉。十五年置潤州，大業初州廢。有句驪山、黃鵠山、蒜山、長塘湖。曲阿有武進縣，梁改爲蘭陵，開皇九年併入。鐘離郡後齊曰西楚州，開皇二年改曰濠州。

translations.literal: Jiangyang was formerly called Guangling; Later Qi established Guangling and Jiangyang commanderies there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year eighteen the county was changed to Hanjiang, and at the beginning of Daye its name was changed to Jiangyang. It had Jiangdu Palace, Yangzi Palace, and Ling Lake. Jiangdu, from Liang through Sui, was sometimes abolished and sometimes established. Hailing had Hailing Commandery established by Liang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Jianling County was also merged into it; soon Jiangpu County was divided off and established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Hailing. Ninghai had Rugao County merged into it at the beginning of Kaihuang. Gaoyou had Zhutang and Sangui counties divided off and established by Liang, and Guangye Commandery was also established; soon, because auspicious grain appeared, it became Shennong Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Zhutang, Sangui, and Linze counties were also merged into it. Anyi had Yangping Commandery and Dongguan Commandery established by Liang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were abolished, and Shibie County was also abolished into it. It had Baima Lake. Shanyang formerly had Shanyang Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year twelve Chuzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. There had been Later Wei's Huaiyin Commandery; Eastern Wei changed it to Huaizhou; Later Qi merged Lu and Fuling to establish Huai'en County; Later Zhou changed it to Shouzhang and also established Dongping Commandery as an immigrant commandery. In Kaihuang year one the commandery was changed to Huaiyin and Chuzhou was also established; soon the commandery was abolished and the county was renamed Huaiyin. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished and the county was merged into Shanyang. Xuyi formerly had Xuyi Commandery established by Wei. Chen established Northern Qiaozhou, which was soon abolished. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Kaocheng, Zhidu, and Yangcheng counties were also merged into it. It had Duliang Mountain. Yancheng had Sheyang Commandery established by Later Qi; Chen changed it to Yancheng; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Qingliu was formerly called Dunqiu and had Xinchang Commandery and Southern Qiaozhou established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed to Chuzhou and the commandery was abolished. Leju and Gaotang counties were also abolished into Dunqiu, which was changed to Xinchang. In year eighteen it was again changed to Qingliu. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Baichan Mountain and Quting Mountain. Quanjiao was called Northern Qiao by Liang, which established Northern Qiao Commandery. Later Qi changed the commandery to Linchu; Later Zhou again called it Northern Qiao. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Chushui. At the beginning of Daye its name was changed. It had Tongguan Mountain and Jiudou Mountain. Luhe was formerly called Weishi and had Qin Commandery established there. Later Qi established Qinzhou. Later Zhou changed the province to Fangzhou and the commandery to Luhe. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year four Weishi was changed to Luhe, and Tangyi and Fangshan counties were abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Later Qi also established Waliang Commandery, which Chen abolished. It had Guabu Mountain and Luhe Mountain. Yongfu was formerly called Pei; Liang established Jingcheng and Dongyang commanderies; Chen abolished the province and combined the two commanderies as Liang Commandery. Later Zhou changed Liang Commandery to Shiliang Commandery, changed Pei County to Shiliang County, and abolished Hengshan County into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the county was changed to Yongfu. It had Xiang Mountain and Yongfu Mountain. Jurong had Mao Mountain, Fu Mountain, and Siping Mountain. Yanling formerly had Southern Xuzhou and Southern Donghai Commandery established there; Liang changed it to Lanling Commandery; Chen again changed it to Donghai. In Kaihuang year nine the province and commandery were both abolished, and Dantu County was also abolished into it. In year fifteen Runzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Goulü Mountain, Huanghu Mountain, Suan Mountain, and Changtang Lake. Qu'e had Wujin County, which Liang changed to Lanling and in Kaihuang year nine merged into Qu'e. Zhongli Commandery was called Western Chuzhou by Later Qi; in Kaihuang year two it was changed to Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 鐘離舊置郡，開皇初郡廢。大業中複置郡。定遠舊曰東城。梁改曰定遠，置臨濠郡。後齊改曰廣安。開皇初郡廢。又有舊九江郡，後齊廢爲曲陽縣，縣尋廢。又有梁置安州，侯景亂廢。化明故曰睢陵，置濟陰郡。後齊改縣曰池南，陳複曰睢陵，後周改爲昭義。開皇初郡廢，大業初縣改名焉。塗山舊曰當塗。後齊改曰馬頭，置郡曰荊山。開皇初改縣曰塗山，廢郡。有當塗山。淮南郡舊曰豫州，後魏曰揚州，梁曰南豫州，東魏曰揚州，陳又曰豫州，後周曰揚州。開皇九年曰壽州，置總管府，大業元年府廢。

translations.literal: Zhongli formerly had a commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. During Daye the commandery was restored. Dingyuan was formerly called Dongcheng. Liang changed it to Dingyuan and established Linhao Commandery. Later Qi changed it to Guang'an. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It also had the old Jiujiang Commandery, which Later Qi abolished to become Quyang County; the county was soon abolished. It also had Anzhou established by Liang, which was abolished during Hou Jing's rebellion. Huaming was formerly called Suiling and had Jiyin Commandery established there. Later Qi changed the county to Chinan; Chen again called it Suiling; Later Zhou changed it to Zhaoyi. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the county's name was changed. Tushan was formerly called Dangtu. Later Qi changed it to Matou and established the commandery as Jingshan. At the beginning of Kaihuang the county was changed to Tushan and the commandery was abolished. It had Dangtu Mountain. Huainan Commandery was formerly called Yuzhou; Later Wei called it Yangzhou; Liang called it Southern Yuzhou; Eastern Wei called it Yangzhou; Chen again called it Yuzhou; Later Zhou called it Yangzhou. In Kaihuang year nine it was called Shouzhou, and a grand administrative office was established; in Daye year one the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 光山舊置光城郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年置縣焉。大業初置光陽郡。又有舊黃川郡，梁廢。樂安梁置宋安郡，及宋安、光城二縣，又有豐安郡，開皇三年並廢入焉。有弋陽山、浮光山、金山、錫山。定城後齊置南郢州，後廢入南、北二弋陽縣，後又省北弋陽入南弋陽，改爲定遠焉。又後魏置弋陽郡，及有梁東新蔡縣。後周改爲淮南郡。又後齊置齊安、新蔡二郡，及廢舊義州，立東光城郡。至開皇初，五郡及郢州並廢。殷城舊曰包信，開皇初改名焉。梁置義城郡及建州，並所領平高、新蔡、新城三郡，開皇初並廢。有大蘇山、南松山。固始梁曰蓼縣。後齊改名焉，置北建州，尋廢州，置新蔡郡。後周改置澮州。開皇初州郡並廢入，又改縣爲固始。有安陽山。期思陳置邊城郡。開皇初郡廢，改縣名焉。有後齊光化郡，亦廢入焉。有大別山。蘄春郡後齊置雍州，後周改曰蘄州。

translations.literal: Guangshan formerly had Guangcheng Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen a county was established there. At the beginning of Daye, Guangyang Commandery was established. It also had the old Huangchuan Commandery, which Liang abolished. Le'an had Song'an Commandery and Song'an and Guangcheng counties established by Liang; it also had Feng'an Commandery, and in Kaihuang year three all were abolished into Le'an. It had Yiyang Mountain, Fuguang Mountain, Jin Mountain, and Xi Mountain. Dingcheng had Southern Yingzhou established by Later Qi; later it was abolished into Southern and Northern Yiyang counties, and later Northern Yiyang was abolished into Southern Yiyang, which was changed to Dingyuan. Later Wei also established Yiyang Commandery, and there was Liang's Eastern Xincai County. Later Zhou changed it to Huainan Commandery. Later Qi also established Qi'an and Xincai commanderies and, abolishing the old Yizhou, established Eastern Guangcheng Commandery. By the beginning of Kaihuang, the five commanderies and Yingzhou were all abolished. Yincheng was formerly called Baoxin and was renamed at the beginning of Kaihuang. Liang established Yicheng Commandery and Jianzhou, together with its subordinate Pinggao, Xincai, and Xincheng commanderies; at the beginning of Kaihuang all were abolished. It had Dasu Mountain and Nansong Mountain. Gushi was called Liao County by Liang. Later Qi changed the name, established Northern Jianzhou, soon abolished the province, and established Xincai Commandery. Later Zhou changed it to establish Huizhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the province and commandery were both abolished into Gushi, and the county was also changed to Gushi. It had Anyang Mountain. Qisi had Biancheng Commandery established by Chen. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. It had Later Qi's Guanghua Commandery, which was also abolished into it. It had Dabie Mountain. Qichun Commandery had Yongzhou established by Later Qi; Later Zhou changed it to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 蘄春舊曰蘄陽，梁改曰蘄水。後齊改曰齊昌，置齊昌郡。開皇十八年改爲蘄春。開皇初郡廢。有安山。浠水舊置永安郡，開皇初郡廢。有石鼓山。蘄水舊曰蘄春，梁改名焉。有鼓吹山。有蘄水。黃梅舊曰永興，開皇初改曰新蔡，十八年改名焉。有黃梅山。羅田梁置義州、義城郡，開皇初並廢。廬江郡梁置南豫州，又改爲合州。

In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Qichun. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had An Mountain. Xishui formerly had Yong'an Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Shigu Mountain. Qishui was formerly called Qichun; Liang changed the name. It had Guchui Mountain and the Qi River. Huangmei was formerly called Yongxing; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed to Xincai, and in year eighteen its name was changed. It had Huangmei Mountain. Luotian had Yizhou and Yicheng Commandery established by Liang; both were abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. Lujiang Commandery had Southern Yuzhou established by Liang, and it was again changed to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 合肥梁曰汝陰，置汝陰郡。後齊分置北陳郡。開皇初郡廢，縣改名焉。廬江齊置廬江郡，梁置湘州，後齊州廢，開皇初郡廢。有冶甫山、上薄山、三公山、聖山、藍家山。襄安梁曰蘄，開皇初改焉。有龜山、紫微山、亞父山、半陽山、白石山、四鼎山。慎東魏置平梁郡，陳曰梁郡，開皇初郡廢。有浮闍山。霍山梁置霍州及岳安郡、岳安縣。後齊州廢。開皇初郡廢，縣改名焉。渒水梁置北沛郡及新蔡縣。開皇初郡廢，又廢新蔡入焉。有墜星山。開化梁置。有衡山、九公山、蹋鼓山、天山、多智山。同安郡梁置豫州，後改曰晉州，後齊改曰江州，陳又曰晉州，開皇初曰熙州。

translations.literal: Hefei was called Ruyin by Liang, which established Ruyin Commandery. Later Qi divided off and established Northern Chen Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. Lujiang had Lujiang Commandery established by Qi; Liang established Xiangzhou; Later Qi abolished the province, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Yefu Mountain, Shangbo Mountain, Sangong Mountain, Sheng Mountain, and Lanjia Mountain. Xiang'an was called Qi by Liang and was changed at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had Gui Mountain, Ziwei Mountain, Yafu Mountain, Banyang Mountain, Baishi Mountain, and Siding Mountain. Shen had Pingliang Commandery established by Eastern Wei; Chen called it Liang Commandery; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Futu Mountain. Huoshan had Huozhou and Yue'an Commandery and Yue'an County established by Liang. Later Qi abolished the province. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. Bishui had Northern Pei Commandery and Xincai County established by Liang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Xincai was also abolished into it. It had Zhuixing Mountain. Kaihua was established by Liang. It had Heng Mountain, Jiugong Mountain, Tagu Mountain, Tian Mountain, and Duozhi Mountain. Tong'an Commandery had Yuzhou established by Liang; later it was changed to Jinzhou; Later Qi changed it to Jiangzhou; Chen again called it Jinzhou; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was called Xizhou.

translations.literal: Huaining formerly had Jinxi Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In Daye year three, Tong'an Commandery was established. Susong had Gaotang Commandery established by Liang. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Gaotang; in year eighteen its name was again changed. It had the Lei River. Taihu was changed to Jinxi at the beginning of Kaihuang and in year eighteen its name was changed back. Wangjiang had Dalei Commandery established by Chen. In Kaihuang year eleven it was changed to Yixiang, and in year eighteen its name was changed. Tong'an was formerly called Zongyang, and Zongyang Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. It had Fudu Mountain. Liyang Commandery had Hezhou established by Later Qi.

translations.literal: Liyang formerly had Liyang Commandery established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was restored.

translations.literal: Wujiang had Jiangdu Commandery established by Liang; Later Qi changed it to Qijiang Commandery, Chen again changed it to Linjiang Commandery, and Zhou changed it to Tongjiang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Liyang Commandery was established. It had Liuhe Mountain. Tongyang Commandery, from Eastern Jin onward, had the commandery there called Yangzhou.

The commandery was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang, and Liyang Commandery was established at the beginning of Daye. It had Liuhe Mountain. When Chen was pacified, Danyang Commandery was also abolished, and Moling, Jiankang, and Tongxia counties were all merged into it. At the beginning of Daye, Danyang Commandery was established. It had Tianmen Mountain and Chu Mountain. Lishui was formerly called Liyang. In Kaihuang year nine Danyang Commandery was abolished into it, and in year eighteen its name was changed. It had Jingting Mountain. Jing had Anwu and Nanyang counties abolished into it when Chen was pacified. It had Gai Mountain and Lingyang Mountain. When Chen was pacified, the province and commandery were both abolished, and its five governed counties, Shicheng, Lincheng, Dingling, Guzhi, and Nanling, were merged into it. Sui'an was formerly called Shifeng; when Chen was pacified, its name was changed. At the end of Liang, Daliang Commandery was established and later changed to Chenliu. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Dade, Guzhang, Anji, and Yuanxiang counties were abolished into it. Piling Commandery had Changzhou established when Chen was pacified.

sentences.zh: 南海舊置南海郡。平陳，郡廢；又分置番禺縣，尋廢入焉。大業初置郡。曲江舊置始興郡。平陳廢，十六年又廢湞陽縣入焉。有玉山、銀山。始興齊曰正階，梁改名焉，又置安遠郡，置東衡州。平陳，改郡置大庾縣，又于此置廣州總管。開皇末移向南海，又十六年廢大庾入焉。翁源梁置，陳又置清遠郡。平陳郡廢。增城舊置東官郡。平陳廢。有羅浮山。寶安樂昌梁置，曰梁化，又分置平石縣。開皇十二年省平石入，十八年改焉。四會舊置綏建郡，又有樂昌郡。平陳，二郡並廢。大業初又並始昌縣入焉。化蒙大業初廢威城縣入焉。清遠舊置清遠郡，又分置威正、廉平、恩洽、浮護等四縣。平陳並廢，以置清遠縣。又齊置齊康郡，至是亦廢入焉。含洭梁置衡州、陽山郡。平陳，州改曰洭州，廢郡。二十年州廢。有堯山。政賓舊置東官郡。平陳，郡廢。懷集新會舊置新會郡。平陳，郡廢，又並盆允，永昌、新建、熙潭、化召、懷集六縣入，爲封州。十一年改爲允州，後又改爲岡州。大業初州廢，並廢封樂縣入。有社山。義寧開皇十年廢新夷、初賓二縣入；又有始康縣，廢入封平。大業初又廢封平入焉。有茂山。龍川郡平陳，置循州總管府。

translations.literal: Nanhai formerly had Nanhai Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished; Fanyu County was also divided off and established, then soon abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye, the commandery was established. Qujiang formerly had Shixing Commandery established there. It was abolished when Chen was pacified, and in year sixteen Zhenyang County was also abolished into it. It had Yu Mountain and Yin Mountain. Shixing was called Zhengjie by Qi; Liang changed the name and also established Anyuan Commandery and Eastern Hengzhou there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was changed and Dayu County was established, and the Guangzhou grand administrative office was also established here. At the end of Kaihuang it was moved toward Nanhai, and in year sixteen Dayu was also abolished into it. Wengyuan was established by Liang, and Chen also established Qingyuan Commandery there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Zengcheng formerly had Dongguan Commandery established there. It was abolished when Chen was pacified. It had Luofu Mountain. Bao'an and Lechang were established by Liang and called Lianghua; Pingshi County was also divided off and established. In Kaihuang year twelve Pingshi was abolished into it, and in year eighteen the name was changed. Sihui formerly had Suijian Commandery and also had Lechang Commandery. When Chen was pacified, the two commanderies were both abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Shichang County was also merged into it. Huameng had Weicheng County abolished into it at the beginning of Daye. Qingyuan formerly had Qingyuan Commandery established there, and Weizheng, Lianping, Enqia, and Fuhu counties were divided off and established. When Chen was pacified, all were abolished and Qingyuan County was established. Qi had also established Qikang Commandery, which by this time was also abolished into it. Hanguang had Hengzhou and Yangshan Commandery established by Liang. When Chen was pacified, the province was changed to Guangzhou and the commandery was abolished. In year twenty the province was abolished. It had Yao Mountain. Zhengbin formerly had Dongguan Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Huaiji and Xinhui formerly had Xinhui Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Penyun, Yongchang, Xinjian, Xitan, Huazhao, and Huaiji counties were also merged into it to make Fengzhou. In year eleven it was changed to Yunzhou and later again changed to Gangzhou. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Fengle County was also abolished into it. It had She Mountain. Yining had Xinyi and Chubin counties abolished into it in Kaihuang year ten; it also had Shikang County, which was abolished into Fengping. At the beginning of Daye, Fengping was also abolished into it. It had Mao Mountain. Longchuan Commandery had the Xunzhou grand administrative office established when Chen was pacified.

sentences.zh: 瀧水舊置開陽縣，置開陽、平原、羅陽等郡。平陳，郡並廢，以名縣。開皇十八年改平原曰瀧水，羅陽縣爲正義。大業初置永熙郡，開陽、正義俱廢入焉。懷德舊曰梁德，置梁德郡。平陳，廢郡。十八年改名懷德。良德陳置，曰務德，後改名焉。安遂梁置建州、廣熙郡，尋廢。州大業初廢。永業梁置永業郡，尋改爲縣，後省。開皇十六年又置。永熙大業初並安南縣入。蒼梧郡梁置成州，開皇初改爲封州。

translations.literal: Longshui formerly had Kaiyang County established there, as well as such commanderies as Kaiyang, Pingyuan, and Luoyang. When Chen was pacified, the commanderies were all abolished and the county was named from them. In Kaihuang year eighteen Pingyuan was changed to Longshui, and Luoyang County became Zhengyi. At the beginning of Daye, Yongxi Commandery was established, and Kaiyang and Zhengyi were both abolished into it. Huaide was formerly called Liangde and had Liangde Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen its name was changed to Huaide. Liangde was established by Chen and called Wude; later its name was changed. Ansui had Jianzhou and Guangxi Commandery established by Liang, which were soon abolished. The province was abolished at the beginning of Daye. Yongye had Yongye Commandery established by Liang; soon it was changed to a county and later abolished. In Kaihuang year sixteen it was established again. Yongxi had Annan County merged into it at the beginning of Daye. Cangwu Commandery had Chengzhou established by Liang; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 始安舊置始安、梁化二郡。平陳，郡並廢。大業初廢興安縣入焉。平樂有目山。荔浦建陵陽朔象隋化義熙舊曰齊熙，置齊熙、黃水二郡及東寧州。平陳，郡並廢。十八年改州曰融州，縣曰義熙。大業初州廢，並廢臨䍧、黃水二縣入焉。龍城梁置。馬平開皇十二年置象州，大業初州廢。桂林大業初並西寧縣入。陽壽有馬平、桂林、象、韶陽等四郡。平陳，並廢。又有淮陽縣，開皇十八年改曰陽寧。大業初省入焉。富川舊置臨賀、樂梁二郡。平陳，並廢，置賀州。大業初州廢，又置臨賀、綏越、蕩山三縣入焉。龍平梁置靜州，梁壽、靜慰二郡。平陳，並廢，又置歸化縣。大業初州廢，又廢歸化、安樂、博勞三縣入焉。豪靜梁置開江、武城二郡，陳置逍遙郡。平陳，郡並廢。又有猛陵、開江二縣，大業初並廢入焉。永平郡平陳，置藤州。

translations.literal: Shi'an formerly had Shi'an and Lianghua commanderies established there. When Chen was pacified, both commanderies were abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Xing'an County was abolished into it. Pingle had Mu Mountain. Lipu, Jianling, Yangshuo, Xiang, Suihua, and Yixi: Yixi was formerly called Qixi and had Qixi and Huangshui commanderies and Eastern Ningzhou established there. When Chen was pacified, the commanderies were both abolished. In year eighteen the province was changed to Rongzhou and the county to Yixi. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Linzang and Huangshui counties were also abolished into it. Longcheng was established by Liang. Maping had Xiangzhou established in Kaihuang year twelve, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Guilin had Xining County merged into it at the beginning of Daye. Yangshou had the four commanderies Maping, Guilin, Xiang, and Shaoyang. When Chen was pacified, all were abolished. It also had Huaiyang County, which in Kaihuang year eighteen was changed to Yangning. At the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Yangshou. Fuchuan formerly had Linhe and Leliang commanderies established there. When Chen was pacified, both were abolished and Hezhou was established. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Linhe, Suiyue, and Dangshan counties were also established into it. Longping had Jingzhou and the two commanderies Liangshou and Jingwei established by Liang. When Chen was pacified, all were abolished, and Guihua County was also established. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Guihua, Anle, and Bolao counties were also abolished into it. Haojing had Kaijiang and Wucheng commanderies established by Liang, and Xiaoyao Commandery established by Chen. When Chen was pacified, the commanderies were all abolished. It also had Mengling and Kaijiang counties, which at the beginning of Daye were both abolished into it. Yongping Commandery had Tengzhou established when Chen was pacified.

sentences.zh: 永平舊置永平郡。平陳，郡廢。大業置郡。武林有燕石山。隋建開皇十九年置。安基梁置建陵郡。平陳，郡廢。隋安開皇十九年置。普甯舊曰陰石，梁置陰石郡。平陳，郡廢，改縣爲奉化。開皇十九年又改名焉。戎成梁置，曰遂成。開皇十一年改名焉。有農山。寧人開皇十五年置，曰安人。十八年改名焉。有壽原山。淳人開皇十九年置。大賓開皇十五年置。賀川開皇十九年置，又陳置建陵、綏越、蒼梧、永建等四郡。平陳，並廢。郁林郡梁置定州，後改爲南定州。

Sui'an was established in Kaihuang year nineteen. Puning was formerly called Yinshi; Liang established Yinshi Commandery there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Fenghua. In Kaihuang year nineteen its name was again changed. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was again established, and Wuping, Longshan, Huaize, and Bushan counties were also abolished into it. sentences.zh: 合浦舊置合浦郡。平陳，郡廢。大業初置郡。南昌北流大業初廢陸川縣入。封山大業初廢廉昌縣入。定川舊立定川郡。平陳，郡廢。龍蘇舊置龍蘇郡。平陳，郡廢。大業初又並大廉縣入。海康梁大通中，割番州合浦立高州，尋又分立合州。大同末，以合肥爲合州，此置南合州。平陳，以此爲合州，置海康縣。大業初州廢，又廢摸落、羅阿、雷川三縣入。抱成舊曰抱，並置郡。平陳，郡廢。十八年改曰抱成。隋康舊曰齊康，置齊康郡。平陳，郡廢，縣改名焉。扇沙舊有椹縣，開皇十八年改爲椹川，大業初廢入。鐵杷開皇十年置。珠崖郡梁置崖州。

Nanchang and Beiliu had Luchuan County abolished into them at the beginning of Daye. Fengshan had Lianchang County abolished into it at the beginning of Daye. Dingchuan formerly had Dingchuan Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Longsu formerly had Longsu Commandery established there. sentences.zh: 欽江舊置宋壽郡。平陳，郡廢。開皇十八年改曰欽江，大業初置寧越郡。安京舊置安京郡。平陳，郡廢。有羅浮山。有武郎江。內亭舊置宋廣郡。平陳，郡廢。十七年改曰新化縣，十八年改名焉。南賓開皇十八年置。遵化開皇二十年置。海安梁置，曰安平，置黃州及寧海郡。平陳，郡廢。十八年改州曰玉州。大業初州廢，其年又省海平、玉山二縣入。交趾郡舊曰交州。

translations.literal: Qinjiang formerly had Songshou Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Qinjiang, and at the beginning of Daye, Ningyue Commandery was established. Anjing formerly had Anjing Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. It had Luofu Mountain and the Wulang River. Neiting formerly had Songguang Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. In year seventeen it was changed to Xinhua County, and in year eighteen its name was changed. Nanbin was established in Kaihuang year eighteen. Zunhua was established in Kaihuang year twenty. Hai'an was established by Liang and called Anping; Huangzhou and Ninghai Commandery were established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen the province was changed to Yuzhou. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and that year Haiping and Yushan counties were also abolished into it. Jiaozhi Commandery was formerly Jiaozhou.

Longbian formerly had Jiaozhi Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Zhuni formerly had Wuping Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Longping was formerly called Wuding and had Wuping Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. In Kaihuang year eighteen the county's name was changed. Pingdao was formerly called Guochang; in Kaihuang year twelve its name was changed. Jiaozhi and Jianing formerly had Xingzhou and Xinchang Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. translations.idiomatic: Anshun was formerly called Changle and was renamed in Kaihuang 16.

translations.idiomatic: Rinan. Rinan Commandery had Dezhou established by Liang and renamed Huanzhou in Kaihuang 18.

translations.literal: Jinning had Lizhou established by Liang. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Zhizhou, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jinning had Lizhou established by Liang, renamed Zhizhou in Kaihuang 18, and abolished at the beginning of Daye.

sentences.zh: 交谷梁置明州，大業初州廢。

translations.literal: Jiaogu had Mingzhou established by Liang; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished.

translations.literal: Guang'an was formerly called Xi'an; in Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. In Bijing Commandery, Linyi was pacified in Daye year one, Dangzhou was established, and soon it was changed to a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'an was formerly called Xi'an and was renamed in Kaihuang 18. Bijing Commandery was created after Linyi was pacified in Daye 1: Dangzhou was established and soon changed to a commandery.

sentences.zh: 揚州于《禹貢》爲淮海之地。

translations.literal: In the "Tribute of Yu," Yangzhou was the land of the Huai and the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the "Tribute of Yu," Yangzhou was the land of the Huai and the sea, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 在天官，自斗十二度至須女七度，爲星紀，於辰在丑，吳、越得其分野。

translations.literal: In the celestial offices, from twelve degrees of Dou to seven degrees of Xuannü is the Star Chronogram asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to chou; Wu and Yue obtained this allotment.
translations.idiomatic: In the celestial offices, from twelve degrees of Dou to seven degrees of Xuannü is the Star Chronogram asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to chou; Wu and Yue obtained this allotment, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 江南之俗，火耕水耨，食魚與稻，以漁獵爲業，雖無蓄積之資，然而亦無饑餒。

translations.literal: The customs south of the Yangzi: fire-plowing and water-weeding, eating fish and rice, taking fishing and hunting as occupations—though without stores of accumulated wealth, yet also without famine.
translations.idiomatic: The customs south of the Yangzi. Fire-plowing and water-weeding, eating fish and rice, taking fishing and hunting as occupations—though without stores of accumulated wealth, yet also without famine.

sentences.zh: 其俗信鬼神，好淫祀，父子或異居，此大抵然也。

translations.literal: Their customs trust ghosts and spirits and delight in excessive sacrifices; fathers and sons sometimes live apart—this is broadly so.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs trust ghosts and spirits and delight in excessive sacrifices; fathers and sons sometimes live apart—this is broadly so, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 江都、弋陽、淮南、鐘離、蘄春、同安、廬江、曆陽，人性並躁勁，風氣果決，包藏禍害，視死如歸，戰而貴詐，此則其舊風也。

translations.literal: Jiangdu, Yiyang, Huainan, Zhongli, Qichun, Tongan, Lujiang, and Liyang—the nature of the people is all impetuous and forceful, the spirit of the region resolute and decisive; they harbor harm, regard death as returning home, and in battle prize deception—this was their old wind.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu, Yiyang, Huainan, Zhongli, Qichun, Tongan, Lujiang, and Liyang—the nature of the people is all impetuous and forceful, the spirit of the region resolute and decisive; they harbor harm, regard death as returning home, and in battle prize deception—this was their old wind, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自平陳之後，其俗頗變，尚淳質，好儉約，喪紀婚姻，率漸於禮。

translations.literal: Since the pacification of Chen, their customs changed considerably; they came to esteem plain simplicity and love frugality; mourning rites and marriage gradually conformed to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Since the pacification of Chen, their customs changed considerably; they came to esteem plain simplicity and love frugality; mourning rites and marriage gradually conformed to ritual, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其俗之敝者，稍愈于古焉。

translations.literal: The defects of their customs were somewhat remedied compared with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The defects of their customs were somewhat remedied compared with antiquity, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 丹陽舊京所在，人物本盛，小人率多商販，君子資于官祿，市厘列肆，埒於二京，人雜五方，故俗頗相類。

translations.literal: Danyang was the site of the old capital; its population was originally abundant. Petty men mostly traded; gentlemen relied on official stipends; market lanes and shops rivaled the two capitals; people mixed from all five directions—hence the customs were quite similar.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang was the site of the old capital; its population was originally abundant. Petty men mostly traded; gentlemen relied on official stipends; market lanes and shops rivaled the two capitals; people mixed from all five directions—hence the customs were quite similar, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 京口東通吳會，南接江湖，西連都邑，亦一都會也。

translations.literal: Jingkou opened eastward to Wu and Kuaiji, connected south to rivers and lakes, and linked west to the capital region—it too was a great metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkou opened eastward to Wu and Kuaiji, connected south to rivers and lakes, and linked west to the capital region—it too was a great metropolis, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其人本並習戰，號爲天下精兵。

translations.literal: Its people from the beginning all practiced warfare and were called the finest troops under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Its people from the beginning all practiced warfare and were called the finest troops under Heaven, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 俗以五月五日爲鬥力之戲，各料強弱相敵，事類講武。

translations.literal: The custom took the fifth day of the fifth month as a contest of strength; each side gauged relative power and matched opponents—much like military drill.
translations.idiomatic: The custom took the fifth day of the fifth month as a contest of strength; each side gauged relative power and matched opponents—much like military drill, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 宣城、毗陵、吳郡、會稽、餘杭、東陽，其俗亦同。

translations.literal: Xuancheng, Piling, Wu, Kuaiji, Yuhang, and Dongyang shared much the same customs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng, Piling, Wu, Kuaiji, Yuhang, and Dongyang shared much the same customs, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 然數郡川澤沃衍，有海陸之饒，珍異所聚，故商賈並湊。

translations.literal: Yet these several commanderies had fertile marshes and plains, rich in land and sea produce, where rare goods gathered—hence merchants all converged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these several commanderies had fertile marshes and plains, rich in land and sea produce, where rare goods gathered—hence merchants all converged, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其人君子尚禮，庸庶敦厖，故風俗澄清，而道教隆洽，亦其風氣所尚也。

translations.literal: Among them, gentlemen honored ritual; common folk were simple and generous—hence customs were clear and Daoist teaching flourished; this too was what the regional spirit held in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, gentlemen honored ritual; common folk were simple and generous—hence customs were clear and Daoist teaching flourished; this too was what the regional spirit held in esteem, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 豫章之俗，頗同吳中，其君子善居室，小人勤耕稼。

translations.literal: The customs of Yuzhang were quite like those of central Wu; its gentlemen were skilled at managing households, its petty men diligent in farming.
translations.idiomatic: The customs of Yuzhang were quite like those of central Wu; its gentlemen were skilled at managing households, its petty men diligent in farming, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 衣冠之人，多有數婦，暴面市廛，競分銖以給其夫。

translations.literal: Men of rank often had several wives who exposed themselves in the marketplaces and competed to divide cash by the fen to supply their husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Men of rank often had several wives who exposed themselves in the marketplaces and competed to divide cash by the fen to supply their husbands, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 及舉孝廉，更要富者，前妻雖有積年之勤，子女盈室，猶見放逐，以避後人。

translations.literal: When nominating filial and incorrupt candidates, they further required wealth; though a first wife had toiled for many years and her children filled the house, she might still be cast out to make way for a successor.
translations.idiomatic: When nominating filial and incorrupt candidates, they further required wealth; though a first wife had toiled for many years and her children filled the house, she might still be cast out to make way for a successor, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: The custom had little litigation but esteemed song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: The custom had little litigation but esteemed song and dance, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 一年蠶四五熟，勤於紡績，亦有夜浣紗而旦成布者，俗呼爲雞鳴布。

translations.literal: Silkworms matured four or five times a year; people were diligent in spinning and weaving; some even washed yarn at night and finished cloth by dawn—the custom called this "cock-crow cloth."
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms matured four or five times a year; people were diligent in spinning and weaving; some even washed yarn at night and finished cloth by dawn—the custom called this "cock-crow cloth."

sentences.zh: 新安、永嘉、建安、遂安、鄱陽、九江、臨川、廬陵、南康、宜春，其俗又頗同豫章，而廬陵人厖淳，率多壽考。

translations.literal: Xin'an, Yongjia, Jian'an, Sui'an, Poyang, Jiujiang, Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun—their customs again resembled Yuzhang considerably, while the people of Luling were simple and honest and mostly lived to great age.
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an, Yongjia, Jian'an, Sui'an, Poyang, Jiujiang, Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun—their customs again resembled Yuzhang considerably, while the people of Luling were simple and honest and mostly lived to great age, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 然此數郡，往往畜蠱，而宜春偏甚。

translations.literal: Yet in these several commanderies people often kept gu poisons, and Yichun was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in these several commanderies people often kept gu poisons, and Yichun was especially severe, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其法以五月五日聚百種蟲，大者至蛇，小者至虱，合置器中，令自相啖，餘一種存者留之，蛇則曰蛇蠱，虱則曰虱蠱，行以殺人。

translations.literal: The method was on the fifth day of the fifth month to gather a hundred kinds of insects, from snakes down to lice, place them together in a vessel, and let them devour one another; the one kind remaining was kept—if a snake, it was called snake gu; if a louse, louse gu—and used to kill people.
translations.idiomatic: The method was on the fifth day of the fifth month to gather a hundred kinds of insects, from snakes down to lice, place them together in a vessel, and let them devour one another; the one kind remaining was kept—if a snake, it was called snake gu; if a louse, louse gu—and used to kill people, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 因食入人腹內，食其五藏，死則其產移入蠱主之家。

translations.literal: Once ingested it entered the person's belly and ate the five viscera; when the victim died, its offspring passed into the gu keeper's household.
translations.idiomatic: Once ingested it entered the person's belly and ate the five viscera; when the victim died, its offspring passed into the gu keeper's household, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 三年不殺他人，則畜者自鐘其弊。

translations.literal: If for three years no one else was killed, the keeper himself would suffer its harm.
translations.idiomatic: If for three years no one else was killed, the keeper himself would suffer its harm, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 累世子孫相傳不絕，亦有隨女子嫁焉。

translations.literal: Generation after generation of descendants transmitted it without end; it could also pass with a woman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation of descendants transmitted it without end; it could also pass with a woman in marriage, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 幹寶謂之爲鬼，其實非也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao called it a ghost, but in fact it was not.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao called it a ghost, but in fact it was not, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自侯景亂後，蠱家多絕，既無主人，故飛游道路之中則殞焉。

translations.literal: After the turmoil of Hou Jing, most gu households died out; with no master, the gu flew along the roads and perished.
translations.idiomatic: After the turmoil of Hou Jing, most gu households died out; with no master, the gu flew along the roads and perished, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自嶺已南二十餘郡，大率土地下濕，皆多瘴厲，人尤夭折。

translations.literal: From south of the Ling Range for more than twenty commanderies, the land was mostly low and damp, all with much miasma; people especially died young.
translations.idiomatic: From south of the Ling Range for more than twenty commanderies, the land was mostly low and damp, all with much miasma; people especially died young, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 南海、交趾，各一都會也，並所處近海，多犀象玳瑁珠璣，奇異珍瑋，故商賈至者，多取富焉。

translations.literal: Nanhai and Jiaozhi were each a great metropolis; both lay near the sea, rich in rhinoceros, elephants, tortoise shell, and pearls—rare and precious goods—hence merchants who came mostly grew wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhai and Jiaozhi were each a great metropolis; both lay near the sea, rich in rhinoceros, elephants, tortoise shell, and pearls—rare and precious goods—hence merchants who came mostly grew wealthy, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其人性並輕悍，易興逆節，椎結踑踞，乃其舊風。

translations.literal: The nature of the people was all lightly fierce; they easily rose in rebellion; topknots and squatting sitting were their old wind.
translations.idiomatic: The nature of the people was all lightly fierce; they easily rose in rebellion; topknots and squatting sitting were their old wind, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其俚人則質直尚信，諸蠻則勇敢自立，皆重賄輕死，唯富爲雄。

translations.literal: The Li people were plain, straight, and trusted in good faith; the various Man were brave and self-reliant—all valued bribes over death and made wealth their heroism.
translations.idiomatic: The Li people were plain, straight, and trusted in good faith; the various Man were brave and self-reliant—all valued bribes over death and made wealth their heroism, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: They dwelled in nests on cliffs and devoted their strength to farming.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelled in nests on cliffs and devoted their strength to farming, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 刻木以爲符契，言誓則至死不改。

translations.literal: They carved wood to make tokens of contract; once words were sworn, they never changed until death.
translations.idiomatic: They carved wood to make tokens of contract; once words were sworn, they never changed until death, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 父子別業，父貧，乃有質身於子。

translations.literal: Fathers and sons had separate estates; if a father was poor, he might even pledge himself to his son.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons had separate estates; if a father was poor, he might even pledge himself to his son, as noted in the geography treatise.
All the Liao were thus.

sentences.zh: 並鑄銅爲大鼓，初成，懸於庭中，置酒以招同類。

translations.literal: They also cast bronze into great drums; when first finished, they hung them in the courtyard and set out wine to summon their kind.
translations.idiomatic: They also cast bronze into great drums; when first finished, they hung them in the courtyard and set out wine to summon their kind, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 來者有豪富子女，則以金銀爲大釵，執以叩鼓，竟乃留遺主人，名爲銅鼓釵。

translations.literal: When guests came with wealthy sons or daughters, they made large hairpins of gold and silver, took them to strike the drum, and finally left them for the host—a thing called "bronze-drum hairpins."
translations.idiomatic: When guests came with wealthy sons or daughters, they made large hairpins of gold and silver, took them to strike the drum, and finally left them for the host—a thing called "bronze-drum hairpins."

sentences.zh: 俗好相殺，多構仇怨，欲相攻則鳴此鼓，到者如雲。

translations.literal: The custom loved mutual killing; many feuds were plotted; when they wished to attack one another they sounded this drum, and those who arrived were like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The custom loved mutual killing; many feuds were plotted; when they wished to attack one another they sounded this drum, and those who arrived were like clouds, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 有鼓者號爲「都老」，群情推服。

translations.literal: Whoever had a drum was called "Du Lao," and the multitude deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever had a drum was called "Du Lao," and the multitude deferred to him, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 本之舊事，尉陀於漢，自稱「蠻夷大酋長、老夫臣」，故俚人猶呼其所尊爲「倒老」也。

translations.literal: Tracing the old matter: Zhao Tuo in Han times styled himself "great chieftain of the Man and Yi, old subject," hence the Li still call those they honor "Dao Lao."
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the old matter. Zhao Tuo in Han times styled himself "great chieftain of the Man and Yi, old subject," hence the Li still call those they honor "Dao Lao."

translations.literal: Through corrupted speech it was again called "Du Lao."
translations.idiomatic: Through corrupted speech it was again called "Du Lao."

sentences.zh: 荊州南郡南郡舊置荊州。

translations.literal: Jingzhou, Nan Commandery: Nan Commandery formerly had Jingzhou established.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou, Nan Commandery. Nan Commandery formerly had Jingzhou established.

sentences.zh: 西魏以封梁爲蕃國，又置江陵總管府。

translations.literal: Western Wei, because Liang was enfeoffed as a vassal state, again established the Jiangling grand administrative office.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei, because Liang was enfeoffed as a vassal state, again established the Jiangling grand administrative office, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era, the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 七年並梁，又置江陵總管，二十年改爲荊州總管。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Liang was annexed; the Jiangling grand administrator was again established; in the twentieth year it was changed to the Jingzhou grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Liang was annexed; the Jiangling grand administrator was again established; in the twentieth year it was changed to the Jingzhou grand administrator, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye it was abolished, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 統縣一十，戸五萬八千八百三十六。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 10 counties with a registered population of 58,836 households.

sentences.zh: 江陵帶南郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初複置郡。長楊開皇八年置，並立睦州，十七年州廢。有宜陽山。宜昌開皇九年置松州，又省歸化、受陵二縣入。十一年州廢，又省宜都縣入。有丹山、黃牛山。枝江當陽後周置平州，領漳川、安遠二郡，屬梁蕃。開皇七年改爲玉州，九年州郡並廢。梁又置安居縣，開皇十八年改曰昭丘，大業初改曰荊台，尋廢入。有清溪山。松滋江左舊置河東郡。平陳，郡廢。有涔水。長林舊曰長寧縣。開皇十一年省長林縣入，十八年改曰長林。公安陳置荊州。開皇九年省孱陵、永安二縣入。有黃山。有靈溪水。安興舊置廣牧縣，開皇十一年省安興縣入，仁壽初改曰安興。又有定襄縣，大業初廢入。紫陵西魏置華陵縣，後周改名焉。其城南面，梁置都州，又置雲澤縣。大業初州縣俱廢入焉。有硤石山。夷陵郡梁置宜州，西魏改曰拓州，後周改曰硤州。

translations.literal: Jiangling carried Nan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. Changyang was established in Kaihuang year eight, and Muzhou was also established; in year seventeen the province was abolished. It had Yiyang Mountain. Yichang had Songzhou established in Kaihuang year nine, and Guihua and Shouling counties were also abolished into it. In year eleven the province was abolished, and Yidu County was also abolished into it. It had Dan Mountain and Huangniu Mountain. Zhijiang and Dangyang had Pingzhou established by Later Zhou, governing Zhangchuan and Anyuan commanderies and belonging to Liang's frontier dependencies. In Kaihuang year seven it was changed to Yuzhou, and in year nine the province and commanderies were both abolished. Liang also established Anju County, which in Kaihuang year eighteen was changed to Zhaoqiu, and at the beginning of Daye was changed to Jingtai; it was soon abolished into Dangyang. It had Qingxi Mountain. Songzi formerly had Hedong Commandery established under the southern dynasties. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. It had the Cen River. Changlin was formerly called Changning County. In Kaihuang year eleven Changlin County was abolished into it, and in year eighteen it was changed to Changlin. Gong'an had Jingzhou established by Chen. In Kaihuang year nine Chanling and Yong'an counties were abolished into it. It had Huang Mountain and the Lingxi River. Anxing formerly had Guangmu County established there. In Kaihuang year eleven Anxing County was abolished into it, and at the beginning of Renshou it was changed to Anxing. It also had Dingxiang County, which was abolished into it at the beginning of Daye. Ziling was established by Western Wei as Hualing County; Later Zhou changed the name. South of its city, Liang established Duzhou and also Yunze County. At the beginning of Daye both province and county were abolished into it. It had Xiashi Mountain. Yiling Commandery had Yizhou established by Liang; Western Wei changed it to Tuozhou; Later Zhou changed it to Xiazhou.

translations.literal: Ziling. Yiling Commandery: Yiling Commandery—in the Liang dynasty, Yizhou was established; Western Wei changed it to Tuozhou; Later Zhou changed it to Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziling. Yiling Commandery. Yiling Commandery—in the Liang dynasty, Yizhou was established; Western Wei changed it to Tuozhou; Later Zhou changed it to Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戸五千一百七十九。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 3 counties with a registered population of 5,179 households.

translations.literal: Yiling carried the commandery seat. It had Ma Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling carried the commandery seat and had Ma Cave.

sentences.zh: 夷道舊置宜都郡，開皇七年廢。有女觀山。

translations.literal: Yidao formerly had Yidu Commandery established there; in Kaihuang year seven it was abolished. It had Nüguan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yidao formerly had Yidu Commandery, abolished in Kaihuang 7. It had Nüguan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遠安舊曰高安，置汶陽郡。又周改縣曰安遠。開皇七年郡廢。竟陵郡舊置郢州。

translations.literal: Yuan'an was formerly called Gao'an and had Wenyang Commandery established there. Zhou also changed the county to Anyuan. In Kaihuang year seven the commandery was abolished. Jingling Commandery formerly had Yingzhou established there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'an was formerly called Gao'an and had Wenyang Commandery. Zhou renamed the county Anyuan, and the commandery was abolished in Kaihuang 7. Jingling Commandery formerly had Yingzhou established there.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戸五萬三千三百八十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 8 counties with a registered population of 53,385 households.

sentences.zh: 長壽後周置石城郡，開皇初郡廢，大業初置竟陵郡。又梁置北新州及梁寧等八郡，後周保定中，州及八郡總管廢入焉。有敖山。藍水宋僑立馮翊郡，蓮勺縣，西魏改郡爲漢東，縣爲藍水。又宋置高陸縣，西魏改曰滶水。開皇初郡廢，大業初省滶水入焉。有唐水。棨川後周置，及置滶川郡。又置清縣，西魏改曰滶陂。開皇初郡廢，大業初省滶陂入焉。漢東齊置，曰上蔡，及置齊興郡。後周郡廢。開皇十八年縣改名焉。有東溫山。清騰梁置，曰梁安，又立崇義郡。後周廢郡。後周又有遂安郡。開皇初廢，七年改名焉。有清騰山。樂鄉舊置武寧郡，西魏置鄀州。又梁置旌陽縣，後改名惠懷，西魏又改曰武山。開皇七年郡廢，大業初州廢，又廢武山入焉。有武陵山。豐鄉西魏置，又置基州及章山郡。開皇七年郡廢，大業初州廢。章山西魏置，曰祿麻，及立上黃郡。開皇七年郡廢，大業初縣改名焉。沔陽郡後周置複州，大業初改曰沔州。

translations.literal: Changshou had Shicheng Commandery established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Jingling Commandery was established. Liang also established Northern Xinzhou and eight commanderies including Liangning; during Later Zhou's Baoding era, the province and the area command of the eight commanderies were abolished into Changshou. It had Ao Mountain. Lanshui had Fengyi Commandery and Lianshao County established as immigrant units by Song; Western Wei changed the commandery to Handong and the county to Lanshui. Song also established Gaolu County, which Western Wei changed to Aoshui. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Aoshui was abolished into it. It had the Tang River. Qichuan was established by Later Zhou, which also established Aochuan Commandery. Qing County was also established; Western Wei changed it to Aobei. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Aobei was abolished into it. Handong was established by Qi and called Shangcai, and Qixing Commandery was established there. Later Zhou abolished the commandery. In Kaihuang year eighteen the county's name was changed. It had Dongwen Mountain. Qingteng was established by Liang and called Liang'an; Chongyi Commandery was also established there. Later Zhou abolished the commandery. Later Zhou also had Sui'an Commandery there. It was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang, and in year seven the name was changed. It had Qingteng Mountain. Lexiang formerly had Wuning Commandery established there, and Western Wei established Ezhou. Liang also established Jingyang County, later renamed Huihuai; Western Wei again changed it to Wushan. In Kaihuang year seven the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Wushan was also abolished into Lexiang. It had Wuling Mountain. Fengxiang was established by Western Wei, which also established Jizhou and Zhangshan Commandery. In Kaihuang year seven the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Zhangshan was established by Western Wei, called Luma, and Shanghuang Commandery was established there. In Kaihuang year seven the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the county's name was changed. Mianyang Commandery had Fuzhou established by Later Zhou; at the beginning of Daye it was changed to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 沔陽梁置沔陽、營陽、州城三郡。西魏省州陵、惠懷二縣，置縣曰建興。後周置複州，後又省營陽、州城二郡入建興。開皇初州移郡廢，仁壽三年複置州。大業初改建興曰沔陽，州廢，複置沔陽郡焉。監利竟陵舊曰霄城，置竟陵郡。後周改縣曰竟陵。開皇初置複州，仁壽三年州複徙建興。又有京山縣，齊置建安郡，西魏改曰光川，後周郡廢。大業初京山縣又廢入焉。甑山梁置梁安郡。西魏改曰魏安郡，置江州，尋改郡曰汶川。後周置甑山縣，建德二年州廢。開皇初郡廢。有陽臺山。漢陽開皇十七年置，曰漢津，大業初改焉。有沌水。沅陵郡開皇九年置辰州。

translations.literal: Mianyang had Mianyang, Yingyang, and Zhoucheng commanderies established by Liang. Western Wei abolished Zhouling and Huihuai counties and established a county called Jianxing. Later Zhou established Fuzhou, and later also abolished Yingyang and Zhoucheng commanderies into Jianxing. At the beginning of Kaihuang the province was moved and the commanderies were abolished; in Renshou year three the province was restored. At the beginning of Daye, Jianxing was changed to Mianyang; the province was abolished, and Mianyang Commandery was restored there. Jianli. Jingling was formerly called Xiaocheng and had Jingling Commandery established there. Later Zhou changed the county to Jingling. At the beginning of Kaihuang Fuzhou was established, and in Renshou year three the province was again moved to Jianxing. It also had Jingshan County, where Qi established Jian'an Commandery; Western Wei changed it to Guangchuan, and Later Zhou abolished the commandery. At the beginning of Daye, Jingshan County was again abolished into it. Zengshan had Liang'an Commandery established by Liang. Western Wei changed it to Wei'an Commandery and established Jiangzhou, then soon changed the commandery to Wenchuan. Later Zhou established Zengshan County, and in Jiande year two the province was abolished. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Yangtai Mountain. Hanyang was established in Kaihuang year seventeen as Hanjin; at the beginning of Daye it was changed. It had the Dun River. Yuanling Commandery had Chenzhou established in Kaihuang year nine.

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 5 counties with a registered population of 4,140 households.

sentences.zh: 沅陵舊置沅陵郡。平陳，郡廢，大業初複。大鄉梁置。鹽泉梁置。龍檦梁置。有武山。辰溪舊曰辰陽。平陳，改名；並廢故夜郎郡，置靜人縣，尋廢。又梁置南陽郡，建昌縣，陳廢縣。開皇初廢郡，置壽州，十八年改爲充州，大業初州廢。有郎溪。武陵郡梁置武州，後改曰沅州。

translations.literal: Yuanling formerly had Yuanling Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. Daxiang was established by Liang. Yanquan was established by Liang. Longbiao was established by Liang. It had Wu Mountain. Chenxi was formerly called Chenyang. When Chen was pacified, the name was changed; the old Yelang Commandery was also abolished and Jingren County was established, then soon abolished. Liang also established Nanyang Commandery and Jianchang County, and Chen abolished the county. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and Shouzhou was established; in year eighteen it was changed to Chongzhou, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Lang Brook. Wuling Commandery had Wuzhou established by Liang, later changed to Yuanzhou.

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 2 counties with a registered population of 3,416 households.

sentences.zh: 武陵舊置武陵郡。平陳，郡廢，並臨沅、沅南、漢壽三縣置武陵縣。大業初複置武陵郡。有望夷山、龍山。

translations.literal: Wuling formerly had Wuling Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Linyuan, Yuannan, and Hanshou counties were combined to establish Wuling County. At the beginning of Daye, Wuling Commandery was restored. It had Wangyi Mountain and Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 龍陽有白查湖。清江郡後周置亭州，大業初改爲庸州。

translations.literal: Longyang had Baicha Lake. In Qingjiang Commandery, Later Zhou established Tingzhou; at the beginning of Daye it was changed to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Longyang had Baicha Lake. Qingjiang Commandery had Tingzhou established by Later Zhou and renamed Yongzhou at the beginning of Daye.

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 5 counties with a registered population of 2,658 households.

sentences.zh: 鹽水後周置縣，並置資田郡，開皇初郡廢，大業初置清江郡。巴山梁置宜都郡、宜昌縣，後周置江州。開皇初置清江縣，十八年改江州爲津州，大業初廢州，省清江入焉。清江後周置施州及清江郡。開皇初郡廢，五年置清江縣，大業初州廢。在陽瞿水。開夷後周置，曰烏飛，開皇初改焉。建始後周置業州及軍屯郡。開皇初郡廢，五年置縣，大業初州廢。襄陽郡江左並僑置雍州。

translations.literal: Yanshui had a county established by Later Zhou, together with Zitian Commandery; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Qingjiang Commandery was established. Bashan had Yidu Commandery and Yichang County established by Liang, and Later Zhou established Jiangzhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang, Qingjiang County was established; in year eighteen Jiangzhou was changed to Jinzhou; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Qingjiang was abolished into it. Qingjiang had Shizhou and Qingjiang Commandery established by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year five Qingjiang County was established; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It was on Yangqu River. Kaiyi was established by Later Zhou and called Wufei; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed. Jianshi had Yezhou and Juntun Commandery established by Later Zhou. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year five the county was established; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Xiangyang Commandery had Yongzhou established there as an immigrant province throughout the southern dynasties.

translations.idiomatic: The grand administrative office was abolished at the start of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戸九萬九千五百七十七。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 11 counties with a registered population of 99,577 households.

sentences.zh: 襄陽帶襄陽郡。開皇初郡廢，大業初複置。有鐘山、峴山、鳳林山。安養西魏置河南郡，後周廢樊城。山都二縣入，開皇初郡廢焉。穀城舊曰義城，置義城郡。後周廢郡，開皇十八年改縣名焉。又梁有築陽，開皇初廢，又梁有興國，義城二郡，並西魏廢。有穀城山、闕林山。上洪宋僑立略陽縣，梁又立德廣郡。西魏改縣曰上洪。開皇初郡廢。又梁置新野郡，西魏改曰威寧，後周廢。有亞山。率道梁置。漢南宋曰華山，置華山郡。西魏改縣爲漢南，屬宜城郡。後周廢武建郡及惠懷、石樑、歸仁、鄢等四縣入，後省宜城郡入武泉。又梁置秦南郡，後周並武泉縣俱廢。有石樑山。陰城西魏置酂城郡，後周廢。又梁置南陽郡，西魏改爲山都郡，後周省。義清梁置，曰穰縣。西魏改爲義清，屬歸義郡。後周廢郡及左安、開南、歸仁三縣入焉。又有武泉郡，開皇初廢。有柤山、靈山。有檀溪水、襄水。南漳西魏並新安、武昌、武平、安武、建平五縣置，初曰重陽，又立南襄陽郡。後周置沮州，尋廢，複改重陽縣曰思安。開皇初郡廢，十八年改縣曰南漳。有荊山。常平西魏置，曰義安，置長湖郡，後改縣曰常平。開皇初郡廢。又後魏置旱停縣，大業初廢。鄀舂陵郡後魏置南荊州，西魏改曰昌州。

translations.literal: Xiangyang carried Xiangyang Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. It had Zhong Mountain, Xian Mountain, and Fenglin Mountain. Anyang had Henan Commandery established by Western Wei; Later Zhou abolished Fancheng and Shandu counties into it, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Gucheng was formerly called Yicheng and had Yicheng Commandery established there. Later Zhou abolished the commandery, and in Kaihuang year eighteen the county's name was changed. Liang also had Zhuyang, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang; Liang also had Xingguo and Yicheng commanderies, both abolished by Western Wei. It had Gucheng Mountain and Quelin Mountain. Shanghong had Lüeyang County established by Song as an immigrant county; Liang also established Deguang Commandery. Western Wei changed the county to Shanghong. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Liang also established Xinye Commandery, which Western Wei changed to Weining; Later Zhou abolished it. It had Ya Mountain. Shuaidao was established by Liang. Hannan was called Huashan by Song, which established Huashan Commandery there. Western Wei changed the county to Hannan, belonging to Yicheng Commandery. Later Zhou abolished Wujian Commandery and Huaihuai, Shiliang, Guiren, and Yan counties into it, and later abolished Yicheng Commandery into Wuquan. Liang also established Qinnan Commandery, and Later Zhou abolished it together with Wuquan County. It had Shiliang Mountain. Yincheng had Zancheng Commandery established by Western Wei, which Later Zhou abolished. Liang also established Nanyang Commandery; Western Wei changed it to Shandu Commandery, and Later Zhou abolished it. Yiqing was established by Liang as Rang County. Western Wei changed it to Yiqing, belonging to Guiyi Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and Zuo'an, Kainan, and Guiren counties into it. It also had Wuquan Commandery, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had Zha Mountain and Ling Mountain. It had Tanxi River and the Xiang River. Nanzhang was established by Western Wei by merging Xin'an, Wuchang, Wuping, Anwu, and Jianping counties; it was first called Chongyang, and Southern Xiangyang Commandery was also established. Later Zhou established Juzhou, soon abolished it, and again changed Chongyang County to Si'an. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county was changed to Nanzhang. It had Jing Mountain. Changping was established by Western Wei and called Yi'an, with Changhu Commandery established there; later the county was changed to Changping. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Later Wei had also established Hanting County, which was abolished at the beginning of Daye. E and Chongling Commandery had Southern Jingzhou established by Later Wei; Western Wei changed it to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 棗陽舊曰廣昌，並置廣昌郡。開皇初郡廢，仁壽元年縣改名焉。大業初置舂陵郡。又西魏置東荊州，尋廢。有霸山。有溲水。舂陵舊置安昌郡，開皇初郡廢。又後魏置豐良縣，大業初廢。有石鼓山。有四望水。清潭有大洪山。有淯水。湖陽後魏置西淮安郡及南襄州，後郡廢，州改爲南平州。西魏改曰升州，後又改曰湖州。後周改置升平郡。開皇初郡廢。仁壽初改曰升州，大業初州廢。又後魏置順陽郡，西魏改爲柘林郡。後周省郡，改縣曰柘林。大業初縣廢入焉。有蓼山。上馬後魏置，曰石馬，後訛爲上馬，因改焉。有鐘離縣，置洞州、洞川郡。後周州廢，開皇初郡廢。十八年改鐘離曰洞川縣，大業初廢入焉。蔡陽梁置蔡陽郡，後魏置南雍州。西魏改曰蔡州，分置南陽縣，後改曰雙泉；又置千金郡、瀴源縣。開皇初郡並廢，大業初州廢，雙泉、瀴源二縣並廢入焉。有唐子山、大鼓山。有瀴水。漢東郡西魏置并州，後改曰隋州。

translations.literal: Zaoyang was formerly called Guangchang, and Guangchang Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in Renshou year one the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye, Chongling Commandery was established. Western Wei also established Eastern Jingzhou, which was soon abolished. It had Ba Mountain and the Sou River. Chongling formerly had Anchang Commandery established there; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Later Wei also established Fengliang County, which was abolished at the beginning of Daye. It had Shigu Mountain and the Siwang River. Qingtan had Dahong Mountain and the Yu River. Huyang had Western Huai'an Commandery and Southern Xiangzhou established by Later Wei; later the commandery was abolished and the province was changed to Southern Pingzhou. Western Wei changed it to Shengzhou, and later again changed it to Huzhou. Later Zhou changed it to establish Shengping Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Renshou it was changed to Shengzhou, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Later Wei also established Shunyang Commandery, which Western Wei changed to Zhelin Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery and changed the county to Zhelin. At the beginning of Daye the county was abolished into Huyang. It had Liao Mountain. Shangma was established by Later Wei as Shima; later this was corrupted to Shangma, so the name was changed. It had Zhongli County, where Dongzhou and Dongchuan Commandery were established. Later Zhou abolished the province, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen Zhongli was changed to Dongchuan County, which at the beginning of Daye was abolished into Shangma. Caiyang had Caiyang Commandery established by Liang, and Later Wei established Southern Yongzhou. Western Wei changed it to Caizhou, divided off and established Nanyang County, later changed it to Shuangquan, and also established Qianjin Commandery and Yingyuan County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were all abolished; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Shuangquan and Yingyuan counties were both abolished into it. It had Tangzi Mountain, Dagu Mountain, and the Ying River. Handong Commandery had Bingzhou established by Western Wei; later it was changed to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋舊置隨郡，西魏又析置㵐西郡及㵐西縣。梁又置曲陵郡。開皇初郡並廢。大業初廢㵐西縣，尋置漢東郡。土山梁曰龍巢，置土州、東西二永甯、真陽三郡，及置石武縣。後周廢三郡爲齊郡，改龍巢曰左陽；又有阜陵縣，改爲漳川縣。開皇初郡廢。十八年改左陽爲真陽，石武爲宜人。大業初又改真陽爲土山，州及宜人、漳川並廢入焉。唐城後魏曰㵐西，置義陽郡。西魏改㵐西爲下溠，又立肆州，尋曰唐州。後周省均、款、溳、歸四州入，改曰唐州。又有東魏南豫州，至是改爲㵐川郡，又置清嘉縣。開皇初郡並廢。十六年改下溠曰唐城，大業初州及諸縣並廢入焉。有清臺山。有㵐水。安貴梁置，曰定陽，又置北郢州。西魏改定陽曰安貴，改北郢州爲款州，又尋廢爲溳水郡，別置戟城郡及戟城縣。後廢戟城郡，改戟城縣曰橫山。開皇初溳水郡廢，大業初又廢橫山縣入焉。順義梁置北隨郡。西魏改爲南陽，析置淮南郡；以厲城、順義二縣立冀州，尋改爲順州；又置安化縣。開皇初郡並廢，十八年改安化曰寧化。大業初州廢，改厲城爲順義，其舊順義及寧化，並廢入焉。有浮山。平林梁置上明郡，開皇初廢。有漂水。上明西魏置，曰洛平縣，開皇十八年改名焉。有鸚鵡山。光化舊曰安化，西魏改爲新化，後周又改焉。安陸郡梁置南司州，尋罷。

translations.literal: Sui formerly had Sui Commandery established there; Western Wei also divided off and established Shenxi Commandery and Shenxi County. Liang also established Quling Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were all abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Shenxi County was abolished, and soon Handong Commandery was established. Tushan was called Longchao by Liang, which established Tuzhou, the three commanderies Eastern Yongning, Western Yongning, and Zhenyang, and Shiwu County. Later Zhou abolished the three commanderies to make Qi Commandery and changed Longchao to Zuoyang; it also had Fuling County, changed to Zhangchuan County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year eighteen Zuoyang was changed to Zhenyang and Shiwu to Yiren. At the beginning of Daye, Zhenyang was again changed to Tushan, and the province, Yiren, and Zhangchuan were all abolished into it. Tangcheng was called Shenxi by Later Wei, which established Yiyang Commandery there. Western Wei changed Shenxi to Xiacuo and also established Sizhou, soon called Tangzhou. Later Zhou abolished Jun, Kuan, Yun, and Gui provinces into it and changed it to Tangzhou. There was also Eastern Wei's Southern Yuzhou, which by this time was changed to Shenchuan Commandery, and Qingjia County was also established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were all abolished. In year sixteen Xiacuo was changed to Tangcheng, and at the beginning of Daye the province and the various counties were all abolished into it. It had Qingtai Mountain and the Shen River. Angui was established by Liang as Dingyang, and Northern Yingzhou was also established. Western Wei changed Dingyang to Angui, changed Northern Yingzhou to Kuanzhou, and soon abolished it to become Yunshui Commandery, separately establishing Jicheng Commandery and Jicheng County. Later Jicheng Commandery was abolished, and Jicheng County was changed to Hengshan. At the beginning of Kaihuang, Yunshui Commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Hengshan County was also abolished into Angui. Shunyi had Northern Sui Commandery established by Liang. Western Wei changed it to Nanyang and divided off Huainan Commandery; with Licheng and Shunyi counties, it established Jizhou, soon changed to Shunzhou; it also established Anhua County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commanderies were all abolished, and in year eighteen Anhua was changed to Ninghua. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, Licheng was changed to Shunyi, and the old Shunyi and Ninghua were both abolished into it. It had Fu Mountain. Pinglin had Shangming Commandery established by Liang, which was abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It had the Piao River. Shangming was established by Western Wei as Luoping County; in Kaihuang year eighteen the name was changed. It had Yingwu Mountain. Guanghua was formerly called Anhua; Western Wei changed it to Xinhua, and Later Zhou changed it again. Anlu Commandery had Southern Sizhou established by Liang, which was soon abolished.
