sentences.zh: 巴陵舊置巴陵郡。平陳，郡廢，大業初複置郡。華容舊曰安南，梁置南安湘郡，尋廢。開皇十八年縣改名焉。沅江梁置，曰藥山，仍爲郡。平陳，郡廢，縣改曰安樂，十八年改曰沅江。湘陰梁置岳陽郡及羅州，陳廢州。平陳，廢郡及湘陰入岳陽縣，置玉州。尋改岳陽爲湘陰，廢玉山縣入焉。十二年廢玉州。羅開皇九年廢吳昌、湘濱二縣入。有渭水、汨水。長沙郡舊置湘州，平陳置潭州總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Baling formerly had Baling Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye the commandery was restored. Huarong was formerly called Annan; Liang established Nan'anxiang Commandery, which was soon abolished. In Kaihuang year eighteen the county's name was changed. Yuanjiang was established by Liang and called Yaoshan, and still served as a commandery. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Anle; in year eighteen it was changed to Yuanjiang. Xiangyin had Yueyang Commandery and Luozhou established by Liang; Chen abolished the province. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished and Xiangyin was merged into Yueyang County, and Yuzhou was established. Soon Yueyang was changed to Xiangyin, and Yushan County was abolished into it. In year twelve Yuzhou was abolished. Luo had Wuchang and Xiangbin counties abolished into it in Kaihuang year nine. It had the Wei River and Mi River. Changsha Commandery formerly had Xiangzhou established there; when Chen was pacified the Tanzhou grand administrative office was established, and at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

translations.literal: Luo. Changsha Commandery: Changsha Commandery formerly had Xiang Province established; when Chen was pacified, the Tanzhou grand administrative office was established; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Luo. Changsha Commandery. Changsha Commandery formerly had Xiang Province established; when Chen was pacified, the Tanzhou grand administrative office was established; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戸一萬四千二百七十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 4 counties with a registered population of 14,275 households.

sentences.zh: 長沙舊曰臨湘，置長沙郡。平陳，郡廢，縣改名焉。有銅山、錫山。衡山舊置衡陽郡。平陳，郡廢，並衡山、湘鄉、湘西三縣入焉。益陽平陳，並新康縣入焉。有浮梁山。邵陽舊置邵陵郡。平陳，郡廢，並扶夷、都梁二縣入焉。衡山郡平陳，置衡州。

translations.literal: Changsha was formerly called Linxiang and had Changsha Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished and the county's name was changed. It had Tong Mountain and Xi Mountain. Hengshan formerly had Hengyang Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Hengshan, Xiangxiang, and Xiangxi counties were all merged into it. Yiyang had Xinkang County merged into it when Chen was pacified. It had Fuliang Mountain. Shaoyang formerly had Shaoling Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Fuyi and Duliang counties were merged into it. Hengshan Commandery had Hengzhou established when Chen was pacified.

translations.literal: Shaoyang. Hengshan Commandery: Hengshan Commandery—when Chen was pacified, Hengzhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang. Hengshan Commandery. Hengshan Commandery—when Chen was pacified, Hengzhou was established.
The commandery governed 4 counties with a registered population of 5,068 households.

sentences.zh: 衡陽舊置湘東郡。平陳，郡廢，並省臨烝、新城、重安三縣入焉。有衡山、武水、連水。洡陰舊曰洡陽。平陳，改名焉。有肥水、酃水。湘潭平陳，廢茶陵、攸水、陰山、建寧四縣入焉。有武陽山。有曆水。新甯有宜溪水、舂江。桂陽郡平陳，置郴州。

translations.literal: Hengyang formerly had Xiangdong Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Linzheng, Xincheng, and Chong'an counties were all abolished into it. It had Heng Mountain, the Wu River, and the Lian River. Leiyin was formerly called Leiyang. When Chen was pacified, the name was changed. It had the Fei River and Ling River. Xiangtan had Chaling, Youshui, Yinshan, and Jianning counties abolished into it when Chen was pacified. It had Wuyang Mountain and the Li River. Xinning had Yixi Brook and Chong River. Guiyang Commandery had Chenzhou established when Chen was pacified.

translations.idiomatic: Xining. Guiyang Commandery. Guiyang Commandery—when Chen was pacified, Chenzhou was established.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戸四千六百六十六。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 3 counties with a registered population of 4,666 households.

sentences.zh: 郴舊置桂陽郡。平陳，郡廢，大業初複置。有萬歲山。有溱水。

translations.literal: Chen formerly had Guiyang Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished; at the beginning of Daye it was restored. It had Wansui Mountain and the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Chen formerly had Guiyang Commandery. It was abolished when Chen was pacified and restored at the beginning of Daye. It had Wansui Mountain and the Qin River.
Linwu had Huayin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 盧陽陳置盧陽郡。平陳，郡廢。有淥水。零陵郡平陳初，置永州總管府，尋廢府。

translations.literal: Luyang had Luyang Commandery established by Chen. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. It had the Lu River. In Lingling Commandery, at the beginning of the pacification of Chen, the Yongzhou grand administrative office was established; soon the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Luyang had Luyang Commandery under Chen; when Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. It had the Lu River. Lingling Commandery had the Yongzhou grand administrative office established at the beginning of the pacification of Chen, but the office was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 統縣五，戸六千八百四十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 5 counties with a registered population of 6,845 households.

sentences.zh: 零陵舊曰泉陵，置零陵郡。平陳，郡廢，又廢應陽、永昌、祁陽三縣入焉。大業初複置郡。湘源平陳，廢洮陽、灌陽、零陵三縣置縣。有黃華山。有觀水、湘水、洮水。永陽舊曰營陽，梁置永陽郡。平陳，郡廢，並營浦、謝沐二縣入焉。營道平陳，並冷道、舂陵二縣入。有九疑山、營山。馮乘有馮水。熙平郡平陳，置連州。

translations.literal: Lingling was formerly called Quanling and had Lingling Commandery established there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Yingyang, Yongchang, and Qiyang counties were also abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was restored. Xiangyuan was established as a county when Chen was pacified by abolishing Taoyang, Guanyang, and Lingling counties. It had Huanghua Mountain and the Guan, Xiang, and Tao rivers. Yongyang was formerly called Yingyang; Liang established Yongyang Commandery there. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and Yingpu and Xiemu counties were merged into it. Yingdao had Lengdao and Chongling counties merged into it when Chen was pacified. It had Jiuyi Mountain and Ying Mountain. Fengcheng had the Feng River. Xiping Commandery had Lianzhou established when Chen was pacified.

translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng. Xiping Commandery. Xiping Commandery—when Chen was pacified, Lianzhou was established.

sentences.zh: 統縣九，戸一萬二百六十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 9 counties with a registered population of 10,265 households.

sentences.zh: 桂陽梁置陽山郡。平陳，郡廢。大業初置熙平郡。有貞女山、方山。有盧水、洭水。陽山有斟水。連山梁置，曰廣德，隋改曰廣澤，仁壽元年改名焉。有黃連山。宣樂梁置，曰梁樂，並置梁樂郡，平陳，郡廢，十八年改爲宣樂。游安熙平舊置齊樂郡，平陳，郡廢。武化梁置。桂嶺舊曰興安，開皇十八年改名焉。開建梁置南靜郡，平陳，郡廢。

translations.literal: Guiyang had Yangshan Commandery established by Liang. When Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye, Xiping Commandery was established. It had Zhennu Mountain and Fang Mountain. It had the Lu River and Kuang River. Yangshan had the Zhen River. Lianshan was established by Liang as Guangde; Sui changed it to Guangze, and in Renshou year one its name was changed. It had Huanglian Mountain. Xuanle was established by Liang as Liangle, and Liangle Commandery was also established there; when Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen it was changed to Xuanle. You'an and Xiping formerly had Qile Commandery established there; when Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished. Wuhua was established by Liang. Guiling was formerly called Xing'an, and in Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. Kaijian had Nanjing Commandery established by Liang; when Chen was pacified, the commandery was abolished.

translations.literal: The "Documents": "Jing and Hengyang constitute Jing Province."
translations.idiomatic: The "Documents". "Jing and Hengyang constitute Jing Province."

sentences.zh: 上當天文，自張十七度至軫十一度，爲鶉首，於辰在巳，楚之分野。

translations.literal: Corresponding to the heavens above, from seventeen degrees of Zhang to eleven degrees of Zhen is the Quail Head asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to si; it is the allotment of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Corresponding to the heavens above, from seventeen degrees of Zhang to eleven degrees of Zhen is the Quail Head asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to si; it is the allotment of Chu, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: Its customs and products were quite like those of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs and products were quite like those of Yangzhou, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其人率多勁悍決烈，蓋亦天性然也。

translations.literal: Its people were mostly fierce, bold, and resolute—probably also their inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were mostly fierce, bold, and resolute—probably also their inborn nature, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 南郡、夷陵、竟陵、沔陽、沅陵、清江、襄陽、舂陵、漢東、安陸、永安、義陽、九江、江夏諸郡，多雜蠻左，其與夏人雜居者，則與諸華不別。

translations.literal: Nan, Yiling, Jingling, Mianyang, Yuanling, Qingjiang, Xiangyang, Chunling, Handong, Anlu, Yong'an, Yiyang, Jiujiang, and Jiangxia commanderies mostly mixed with Man on the left; those who lived intermingled with Han people were indistinguishable from the various Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Nan, Yiling, Jingling, Mianyang, Yuanling, Qingjiang, Xiangyang, Chunling, Handong, Anlu, Yong'an, Yiyang, Jiujiang, and Jiangxia commanderies mostly mixed with Man on the left; those who lived intermingled with Han people were indistinguishable from the various Hua, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其僻處山谷者，則言語不通，嗜好居處全異，頗與巴、渝同俗。

translations.literal: Those dwelling secluded in mountain valleys had unintelligible speech and wholly different tastes and dwellings—quite the same customs as Ba and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Those dwelling secluded in mountain valleys had unintelligible speech and wholly different tastes and dwellings—quite the same customs as Ba and Yu, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻本其所出，承盤瓠之後，故服章多以班布爲飾。

translations.literal: The various Man originally sprang from there, inheriting from Panhu afterward—hence their dress and adornments mostly used patterned cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The various Man originally sprang from there, inheriting from Panhu afterward—hence their dress and adornments mostly used patterned cloth, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: To address one another as "Man" was a deep taboo.
translations.idiomatic: To address one another as "Man" was a deep taboo, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏南遷之後，南郡、襄陽，皆爲重鎮，四方湊會，故益多衣冠之緒，稍尚禮義經籍焉。

translations.literal: After the Jin house moved south, Nan Commandery and Xiangyang both became strategic strongholds where people gathered from all directions—hence there were ever more lines of gentry and officials, and they slightly came to honor ritual, righteousness, and the classics.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin house moved south, Nan Commandery and Xiangyang both became strategic strongholds where people gathered from all directions—hence there were ever more lines of gentry and officials, and they slightly came to honor ritual, righteousness, and the classics, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 九江襟帶所在，江夏、竟陵、安陸，各置名州，爲籓鎮重寄，人物乃與諸郡不同。

translations.literal: Jiujiang was the strategic hinge; Jiangxia, Jingling, and Anlu each had famous provinces as weighty posts of frontier defense—their people differed from the other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang was the strategic hinge; Jiangxia, Jingling, and Anlu each had famous provinces as weighty posts of frontier defense—their people differed from the other commanderies, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 大抵荊州率敬鬼，尤重祠祀之事，昔屈原爲製《九歌》，蓋由此也。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, Jing Province mostly revered ghosts and especially valued sacrificial affairs; in old times Qu Yuan composed the "Nine Songs"—probably from this.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Jing Province mostly revered ghosts and especially valued sacrificial affairs; in old times Qu Yuan composed the "Nine Songs"—probably from this, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 屈原以五月望日赴汨羅，土人追到洞庭不見，湖大船小，莫得濟者，乃歌曰：「何由得渡湖！」

translations.literal: On the full moon of the fifth month Qu Yuan went to the Miluo; local people pursued him to Dongting but did not see him; the lake was large and the boats small, and none could cross—so they sang: "How can we cross the lake!"
translations.idiomatic: On the full moon of the fifth month Qu Yuan went to the Miluo; local people pursued him to Dongting but did not see him; the lake was large and the boats small, and none could cross—so they sang. "How can we cross the lake!"

sentences.zh: 因爾鼓棹爭歸，競會亭上，習以相傳，爲競渡之戲。

translations.literal: Then they raced their oars homeward, gathering at pavilions; the practice was handed down and became the sport of racing boats.
translations.idiomatic: Then they raced their oars homeward, gathering at pavilions; the practice was handed down and became the sport of racing boats, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其迅楫齊馳，棹歌亂響，喧振水陸，觀者如雲，諸郡率然，而南郡、襄陽尤甚。

translations.literal: Swift oars flew together, boat songs rang in confusion, shaking water and land; spectators were like clouds—all commanderies did so, but Nan Commandery and Xiangyang especially.
translations.idiomatic: Swift oars flew together, boat songs rang in confusion, shaking water and land; spectators were like clouds—all commanderies did so, but Nan Commandery and Xiangyang especially, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 二郡又有牽鉤之戲，云從講武所出，楚將伐吳，以爲教戰，流遷不改，習以相傳。

translations.literal: The two commanderies also had the sport of pulling hooks, said to come from military drill: a Chu general about to attack Wu used it to teach warfare; the practice flowed on unchanged and was handed down.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanderies also had the sport of pulling hooks, said to come from military drill. A Chu general about to attack Wu used it to teach warfare; the practice flowed on unchanged and was handed down.

sentences.zh: 鉤初發動，皆有鼓節，群噪歌謠，振驚遠近，俗云以此厭勝，用致豐穰。

translations.literal: When the hook first moved, there were drum beats; crowds shouted songs, startling far and near; popularly they said this overcame evil to bring abundant harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When the hook first moved, there were drum beats; crowds shouted songs, startling far and near; popularly they said this overcame evil to bring abundant harvest, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: The practice also spread to other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The practice also spread to other commanderies, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文之臨雍部，發教禁之，由是頗息，其死喪之紀，雖無被髪袒踴，亦知號叫哭泣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang governed Yong Region, he issued an edict forbidding it; thereby it largely ceased. In their rites of death and mourning, though without disheveled hair and bared shoulders, they still knew shouting and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang governed Yong Region, he issued an edict forbidding it; thereby it largely ceased. In their rites of death and mourning, though without disheveled hair and bared shoulders, they still knew shouting and weeping, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 始死，即出屍於中庭，不留室內。

translations.literal: At first death the corpse was immediately taken out to the central courtyard and not kept indoors.
translations.idiomatic: At first death the corpse was immediately taken out to the central courtyard and not kept indoors, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 斂畢，送到山中，以十三年爲限。

translations.literal: When encoffining was complete, it was sent to the mountains, with thirteen years as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: When encoffining was complete, it was sent to the mountains, with thirteen years as the limit, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 先擇吉日，改入小棺，謂之拾骨。

translations.literal: First an auspicious day was chosen; the bones were transferred to a small coffin—this was called "gathering the bones."
translations.idiomatic: First an auspicious day was chosen; the bones were transferred to a small coffin—this was called "gathering the bones."

sentences.zh: 拾骨必須女婿，蠻重女婿，故以委之。

translations.literal: Gathering the bones had to be done by the son-in-law; the Man greatly valued sons-in-law, hence this was entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering the bones had to be done by the son-in-law; the Man greatly valued sons-in-law, hence this was entrusted to them, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 拾骨者，除肉取骨，棄小取大。

translations.literal: The bone-gatherers removed the flesh and took the bones, discarding small ones and keeping large ones.
translations.idiomatic: The bone-gatherers removed the flesh and took the bones, discarding small ones and keeping large ones, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 當葬之夕，女婿或三數十人，集會于宗長之宅，著芒心接籬，名曰茅綏。

translations.literal: On the night of burial, sons-in-law—sometimes several tens—gathered at the clan elder's house, wearing mang-fiber heart caps and bamboo hats, called "Mao Sui."
translations.idiomatic: On the night of burial, sons-in-law—sometimes several tens—gathered at the clan elder's house, wearing mang-fiber heart caps and bamboo hats, called "Mao Sui."

sentences.zh: 各執竹竿，長一丈許，上三四尺許，猶帶枝葉。

translations.literal: Each held a bamboo pole about one zhang long, three or four chi at the top still bearing branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Each held a bamboo pole about one zhang long, three or four chi at the top still bearing branches and leaves, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其行伍前卻，皆有節奏，歌吟叫呼，亦有章典。

translations.literal: Their ranks advancing and retreating all had rhythm; singing, chanting, and shouting also had fixed patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Their ranks advancing and retreating all had rhythm; singing, chanting, and shouting also had fixed patterns, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 傳云盤瓠初死，置之於樹，乃以竹木刺而下之，故相承至今，以爲風俗。

translations.literal: Tradition says when Panhu first died he was placed in a tree; then bamboo and wood were used to pierce and bring him down—hence handed down to the present as custom.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says when Panhu first died he was placed in a tree; then bamboo and wood were used to pierce and bring him down—hence handed down to the present as custom, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: They concealed the matter and called it "piercing the Northern Dipper."
translations.idiomatic: They concealed the matter and called it "piercing the Northern Dipper."

sentences.zh: 既葬設祭，則親疏咸哭，哭畢，家人既至，但歡飲而歸，無複祭哭也。

translations.literal: After burial and sacrifice, kin near and far all wept; when weeping ended and the family had arrived, they merely drank in joy and returned—there was no further sacrificial weeping.
translations.idiomatic: After burial and sacrifice, kin near and far all wept; when weeping ended and the family had arrived, they merely drank in joy and returned—there was no further sacrificial weeping, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其左人則又不同，無衰服，不復魄。

translations.literal: The Zuo people were again different: no mourning garments, no soul-recalling rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo people were again different. No mourning garments, no soul-recalling rites.

sentences.zh: 始死，置屍館舍，鄰里少年，各持弓箭，繞屍而歌，以箭扣弓爲節。

translations.literal: At first death the corpse was placed in a lodge; youths of the neighborhood each held bow and arrow and circled the corpse singing, beating the bow with the arrow as rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: At first death the corpse was placed in a lodge; youths of the neighborhood each held bow and arrow and circled the corpse singing, beating the bow with the arrow as rhythm, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其歌詞說平生樂事，以到終卒，大抵亦猶今之挽歌。

translations.literal: The song lyrics told pleasures of a lifetime up to the final end— broadly like today's elegies.
translations.idiomatic: The song lyrics told pleasures of a lifetime up to the final end— broadly like today's elegies, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 歌數十闋，乃衣衾棺斂，送往山林，別爲廬舍，安置棺柩。

translations.literal: After dozens of stanzas they clothed and coffined the body and sent it to the mountains, separately making a hut to place the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of stanzas they clothed and coffined the body and sent it to the mountains, separately making a hut to place the coffin, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 亦有於村側瘞之，待二三十喪，總葬石窟。

translations.literal: Some also buried at the village side; after twenty or thirty funerals they were collectively interred in stone caves.
translations.idiomatic: Some also buried at the village side; after twenty or thirty funerals they were collectively interred in stone caves, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 長沙郡又雜有夷蜒，名曰莫徭，自云其先祖有功，常免徭役，故以爲名。

translations.literal: Changsha Commandery also mixed with Yiyan, called Mo Yao; they said their ancestors had merit and were permanently exempt from corvée—hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha Commandery also mixed with Yiyan, called Mo Yao; they said their ancestors had merit and were permanently exempt from corvée—hence the name, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其男子但著白布褌衫，更無巾褲；

translations.literal: The men wore only white cloth drawers and jackets, with no caps or trousers;
translations.idiomatic: The men wore only white cloth drawers and jackets, with no caps or trousers;

sentences.zh: 其女子青布衫、班布裙，通無鞋屩。

translations.literal: the women wore blue cloth jackets and patterned cloth skirts, generally without shoes or sandals.
translations.idiomatic: the women wore blue cloth jackets and patterned cloth skirts, generally without shoes or sandals, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: Marriage and betrothal used iron cobalt ore as bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage and betrothal used iron cobalt ore as bride-price, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 武陵、巴陵、零陵、桂陽、澧陽、衡山、熙平皆同焉。

translations.literal: Wuling, Baling, Lingling, Guiyang, Liyang, Hengshan, and Xiping were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling, Baling, Lingling, Guiyang, Liyang, Hengshan, and Xiping were all the same, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其喪葬之節，頗同于諸左云。

translations.literal: Their funeral rites were quite the same as those of the various Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Their funeral rites were quite the same as those of the various Zuo, as noted in the geography treatise.
